candidate: L8: a PKU response with is_safe true and lexicon class REFUSAL-OPENING, in a record whose other response has is_safe false; candidate order = the config's source order, then line, then response index; id = <source>:<line, 6 digits>:<response index> (ANCH's uid)
classifier: no Qwen3Guard or other classifier filters the pool
evaluation_forms: every bank of P (dev, selector, hidden; all splits) and every form of every ARC item, as ANCH's load_evaluation builds them (L9 (1)); the run stops unless the count equals expected_evaluation_forms (L9 (2)); records hold counts per bank and the largest kept score only (L9 (3))
filter_rule: each filter runs on the previous filter's survivors; within one filter a row counts under every reason of that filter it meets and is removed once; N is reported after each filter
filters: 2 control_string: a substring of the union of the config's and P's eligibility.forbidden_substrings in the prompt or the response
3 exact overlap: overlap_with_an_existing_or_evaluation_prompt (the normalized prompt equals a training, query or evaluation form of P); overlap_with_an_anchor_prompt (one of the 128 anchor prompts)

4 near duplicate: near_duplicate_of_evaluation_prompt_<bank> (character 5-gram Jaccard >= max_jaccard with an evaluation form of the bank: dev, selector, hidden; experiments.safety_selection.prepare._NearDuplicates); near_duplicate_of_anchor_prompt
5 encode_train_<error>: encode_train(prompt, response) refuses under REC's model.max_train_tokens
6 generation_prompt_<error>: encode_generation_prompt(prompt) refuses under REC's model.max_prompt_tokens (lead decisions section 3 (1), L11 (5))
7 duplicate_prompt: not the first candidate of its normalized prompt, in candidate order

anch.use: load_config, read_sources (parse_pku after the config's file pins), load_evaluation, validate_list; loaded by path after its SHA-256 check, never run as a script

list_rule: a list is the first size ids of sealed_order(its source ids, its key)

s3_subset.from: the S-pool (overlap with S1 allowed and counted, L10)

s4_candidates.from: the S-pool minus S1 (L11; REQ-9 keeps the first 48 that pass)

max_jaccard_source: the data config's injection.near_duplicate.max_jaccard (refused if it differs)
name: build_s_pool

outputs.full: --full-out, inside a folder named tmp: s_pool.json, s1.json, s3_subset.json, s4_candidates.json, s3_safe.pool.json (REQ-3's pool s3_safe: the S3 subset, then S1's rows outside it, L10 (2))
outputs.record: --out: s_pool_record.json (text-free; each text field as its SHA-256)

report_only: L8: the candidates and the S-pool rows whose record's safer_response_id (separately better_response_id) names the other response, read by line from the hash-checked bytes after parse_pku; a value that is not the integer 0 or 1 refuses. L10: |S1 & S3 subset| beside 48 x 1,000 / N, and |S1 & S4 candidates| = 0
requirement: REQ-6 (brief rev 1 12cbf463; PLAN-S:145-147, :171); lead decisions: L8, L9, L10, L11, section 3 (1); W1-11
stop: counts only, nothing written: N < min_pool after the last filter, a list that cannot be filled, or fewer than decoy_rows S-pool rows outside S1, the S3 subset and the S4 candidates (REQ-8's decoy, W1-09)
w1_11: per S-pool row in the sealed record: source (the PKU file id), line, response_index (taken) and companion_index (the other response, marked unsafe in the bytes)
